subtitle: On the banks of the Krishna, stone remembers many hands.

panels.shot: sweeping wide of the Krishna riverfront with the great stupa rising beyond
panels.action: Amaravati Sculptor-Donor stands in three-quarter profile on the riverbank, chisel and mallet in hand, gazing toward the distant dome and railing of the mahacetiya glimmering in soft light on the horizon.

dialogue.text: On the Krishna at Dharanikota, the mahacetiya of Amaravati grows over centuries—shaped by queens, merchants, monks and sculptors whose stone stories travel far beyond Andhra.

i18n.hi: धरणीकोटा की कृष्णा किनारे, अमरावती का महासेतिय सदियों में बढ़ता है—रानियों, व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं और शिल्पियों की पत्थर कथाएँ आंध्र से दूर तक जाती हैं।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over the Krishna river plain
panels.action: A broad view of the Krishna river curling through fertile fields and scattered villages, with a low mound at Dharanikota hinting at an early stupa amidst simple mud-brick structures and groves of trees.

dialogue.text: Long before dynasties carve their names in stone, a modest mound rises at Dharanikota, a reliquary for the Buddha’s memory on the broad, quiet plains of the Krishna.

i18n.hi: राजघराने पत्थर पर नाम खोदने से बहुत पहले, धरणीकोटा पर एक छोटा टीला उठता है—कृष्णा की शांत, चौड़ी धरती पर बुद्ध स्मृति का स्तूप।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward an early stone railing fragment beside the mound
panels.action: Amaravati Sculptor-Donor, shown as a younger artisan, kneels by rough limestone slabs near the stupa mound, testing the stone with his fingers while monks in simple robes walk in the background.

dialogue.text: Limestone lies close to the surface here. From this pale stone, generations will coax stories—turning a local shrine into the mahacetiya remembered in inscriptions.

i18n.hi: यहाँ सतह के पास चूना पत्थर है। इसी फीके पत्थर से पीढ़ियाँ कहानियाँ निकालेंगी—एक स्थानीय मंदिर को शिलालेखों वाला महासेतिय बना देंगी।

panels.action: Inside a simple riverside shed, Amaravati Sculptor-Donor stands among blocks of limestone; another artisan roughs out a drum slab while a monk points to a palm-leaf sketch of a stupa with circumambulatory path.

dialogue.text: Workshops form along the river. Artisans learn to cut drum slabs and railings, listening as monks explain the sacred path around the stupa, where stone and devotion will meet.

i18n.hi: नदी किनारे कार्यशालाएँ बसती हैं। कारीगर ड्रम पट्ट और घाटे काटना सीखते हैं, जबकि भिक्षु बताते हैं स्तूप की परिक्रमा मार्ग, जहाँ पत्थर और भक्ति मिलेंगे।

panels.shot: low-angle view of early donors before a simple railing
panels.action: An early scene shows local merchants and their families beside a plain stone vedika; Amaravati Sculptor-Donor presents a finished slab as a monk gestures toward the stupa mound in blessing.

dialogue.text: The first railings rise through many small gifts. Traders, farmers, craftsmen—each sponsors a piece. The mahacetiya is not one man’s monument, but a web of offerings.

i18n.hi: पहली रेलिंगें छोटे‑छोटे उपहारों से उठती हैं। व्यापारी, किसान, कारीगर—हर कोई एक टुकड़ा देता है। महासेतिय किसी एक की निशानी नहीं, चढ़ावों का जाल है।

panels.shot: transition wide shot showing architectural change
panels.action: A composite wide view shows the stupa at two stages: on one side, a modest dome; on the other, elaborate extensions with taller drum and richer railing, Amaravati Sculptor-Donor standing between, older now, surveying the work.

dialogue.text: Over the centuries, the mound becomes a great drum and dome. Each phase adds rings of stone and railings, reshaping the mahacetiya as new donors and new rulers take interest.

i18n.hi: सदियों में टीला बड़े ड्रम और गुंबद में ढलता है। हर दौर पत्थर की नई परतें और रेलिंगें जोड़ता है, जैसे‑जैसे नए दाता और नए राजा ध्यान देते हैं।

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot in a Satavahana court pavilion
panels.action: In a decorated pavilion near the river, a Satavahana queen and officials receive monks; Amaravati Sculptor-Donor stands respectfully with a carved panel, as attendants fan the royal figure amid banners bearing the Ujjain symbol.

dialogue.text: In Satavahana times, royal women and officials join the circle of patrons. Inscribed names record queens and high officers, yet their donations still mingle with those of humble guilds.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन समय में, राजमहिला और अफ़सर भी दाताओं की मंडली में जुड़ते हैं। शिलालेखों में रानियों और उच्च अधिकारियों के नाम आते हैं, फिर भी उनकी भेंटें साधारण संघों के साथ घुलती‑मिलती हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on hands chiseling intricate relief
panels.action: Amaravati Sculptor-Donor’s hands grip chisel and mallet against pale limestone, carving delicate swirling scrolls and stylized lotus medallions, fine stone dust catching the afternoon light.

dialogue.text: Under steady hands, limestone yields a new language—deep scrolls, rich lotus belts, figures caught mid-gesture. The Amaravati style takes shape, distinct yet speaking the Buddha’s story.

i18n.hi: सधे हाथों से चूना पत्थर नई भाषा देता है—गहरे बेलबूटे, भरी हुई पद्म‑मालाएँ, बीच हरकत पकड़े हुए रूप। अलग‑सी अमरावती शैली बनती है, जो बुद्ध कथा ही सुनाती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of sculptors carving narrative scenes
panels.action: Several sculptors work along a line of drum slabs: one carves a crowded scene of worshippers around an empty throne and Bodhi tree, while Amaravati Sculptor-Donor gestures, guiding composition.

dialogue.text: They rarely show the Buddha as a body. Instead—thrones, footprints, trees, wheels. Devotees pressing in from every side. Absence becomes presence through learned convention and flowing form.

i18n.hi: वे बुद्ध को देह रूप में कम दिखाते हैं। बदले में—सिंहासन, पदचिह्न, वृक्ष, चक्र। हर ओर से झुकते भक्त। शून्यता सीख हुई परंपरा और बहती आकृति से उपस्थिति बन जाती है।

panels.shot: medium shot at an inscription carving
panels.action: Amaravati Sculptor-Donor stands beside a stone post where a scribe carefully incises Brahmi letters recording a donation; a merchant points to the text, his child watching in quiet pride.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions bite into stone beside the images: ‘Gift of the merchant so‑and‑so, of his wife, of the ivory-carvers’ guild.’ Each line fixes ordinary lives into the monument’s skin.

i18n.hi: चित्रों के पास पत्थर पर अक्षर चुभते हैं: ‘अमुक व्यापारी की भेंट, उसकी पत्नी की, दाँत‑काटने वालों के संघ की।’ हर पंक्ति साधारण जीवन को इस स्मारक की त्वचा में बाँध देती है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of the completed stupa complex
panels.action: A panoramic view shows the great Amaravati mahacetiya at its height, with multiple railings, gateways and sculptured slabs encircling the gleaming dome, crowds of monks, nuns and laypeople circumambulating in orderly procession; Amaravati Sculptor-Donor watches from the edge.

dialogue.text: By the early centuries CE, the mahacetiya stands as a jewel on the Krishna—its drum and railings dense with reliefs, its terraces busy with monks, nuns, traders and pilgrims circling in quiet rhythm.

i18n.hi: ईस्वी की शुरुआती सदियों तक, महासेतिय कृष्णा पर रत्न बन खड़ा है—उसका ड्रम और रेलिंगें घनी मूर्तियों से भरी, उसकी परतों पर भिक्षु, भिक्षुणी, व्यापारी और यात्री शांत लय में परिक्रमा करते हैं।

panels.shot: comparative wide shot hinting at connections to other sites
panels.action: A visual montage contrasts a richly carved Amaravati slab with similar reliefs at another stupa site, suggested as Kanaganahalli on the Krishna’s upper reaches, as Amaravati Sculptor-Donor unrolls a sketch before visiting artisans.

dialogue.text: Amaravati’s language of stone echoes upriver and across regions. Sites like Kanaganahalli show kinship in form and theme, tracing networks of monks, donors and craftsmen across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: अमरावती की पत्थर भाषा नदी के ऊपर और दूर प्रदेशों तक गूँजती है। कनगनहल्ली जैसे स्थल रूप और भाव में रिश्तेदारी दिखाते हैं, दक्कन भर में भिक्षुओं, दाताओं और कारीगरों के जाल खींचते हैं।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of weathered reliefs centuries later
panels.action: Centuries on, Amaravati Sculptor-Donor is now only imagined, his figure ghostlike beside worn, lichen-streaked slabs; plants grow through fallen railings as a lone monk walks by in faded robes.

dialogue.text: Time shifts power and faith. Patronage wanes, structures crack, railings fall. Yet even in partial ruin, the sculptures continue to shape how later visitors picture the Buddha’s path.

i18n.hi: समय से सत्ता और श्रद्धा बदलती है। दान घटते हैं, ढाँचे चिरते हैं, रेलिंगें गिरती हैं। फिर भी अधूरी खंडहर में भी मूर्तियाँ बाद के दर्शकों के मन में बुद्ध मार्ग की छवि गढ़ती रहती हैं।

panels.action: British-era officers and Indian assistants stand amid exposed stupa remains; one sketches a relief while another measures a slab. Amaravati Sculptor-Donor appears symbolically in the background, watching as blocks are prepared for removal.

dialogue.text: In the nineteenth century, the ruined mound draws new eyes. Surveyors like James Burgess document the site, while many slabs are lifted and sent to distant museums and Madras collections.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी में, यह टूटा टीला नई निगाहें खींचता है। जेम्स बर्गेस जैसे सर्वेक्षक स्थल दर्ज करते हैं, जबकि कई पट्ट उठाकर दूर संग्रहालयों और मद्रास के संग्रहों में भेजे जाते हैं।

panels.shot: gallery-like wide shot of slabs in a colonial museum hall
panels.action: Inside a high-ceilinged museum gallery, Amaravati drum slabs stand against walls under skylights; a small group of viewers examine the carvings, while Amaravati Sculptor-Donor’s ghostly figure stands between past and present.

dialogue.text: Panels from Amaravati appear in Madras, then in London. Scholars like Robert Knox and later Akira Shimada trace their origins, phases and meanings, piecing together the lost mahacetiya from scattered stone.

i18n.hi: अमरावती के पैनल पहले मद्रास में, फिर लंदन में दिखते हैं। रॉबर्ट नॉक्स और बाद में अकीरा शिमादा जैसे विद्वान उनके स्रोत, दौर और अर्थ पकड़ते हैं, बिखरे पत्थर से खोया महासेतिय जोड़ने की कोशिश करते हैं।

panels.shot: introspective close-up on Amaravati Sculptor-Donor’s face, half in shadow
panels.action: A contemplative close-up shows Amaravati Sculptor-Donor, symbolic and timeless, his expression a mix of pride and melancholy, the reflection of a museum display case faintly visible before him.

dialogue.text: Our hands are gone, but the stone still speaks across rivers and seas.

i18n.hi: हमारे हाथ जा चुके हैं, पर पत्थर अब भी नदियाँ और समुद्र पार बोलता है।

panels.shot: present-day wide shot of Amaravati site and museum
panels.action: A modern view shows the reconstructed stupa base at Amaravati with protective structures, alongside a museum displaying surviving slabs; visitors walk among the exhibits as the river glows in the distance and Amaravati Sculptor-Donor’s presence hovers over the scene.

dialogue.text: Today, Amaravati’s fragments lie in Andhra and abroad. Debates continue about where they belong, yet wherever they rest, they reveal a sanctuary made not by one ruler, but by generations.

i18n.hi: आज अमरावती के टुकड़े आंध्र में भी हैं और विदेशों में भी। वे कहाँ रहें, इस पर बहस चलती है, पर जहाँ भी टिकें, वे दिखाते हैं कि यह धाम किसी एक शासक ने नहीं, पीढ़ियों ने गढ़ा।

panels.shot: final sweeping wide shot along the Krishna at sunset
panels.action: At sunset, the Krishna river shines like molten bronze; Amaravati Sculptor-Donor stands on the bank, silhouetted, with faint outlines of the old stupa and distant museums merging into the sky.

dialogue.text: The Amaravati reliefs endure as a flowing scripture in stone—crafted by queens and guilds, monks and sculptors—reminding us that great art is usually the long labor of many hands across time.

i18n.hi: अमरावती की मूर्तिपट्टी पत्थर में बहती हुई शास्त्र बनकर रहती है—रानियों और संघों, भिक्षुओं और शिल्पियों के हाथों बनी—याद दिलाती है कि महान कला अक्सर समय भर कई हाथों की लंबी मेहनत होती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: On the banks of the Krishna, stone remembers many hands.
subtitle_i18n.hi: कृष्णा के तट पर, पत्थर कई हाथों को याद रखता है।
